# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 61 (Bu-Vb Pc61)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc61
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 61
**Title (English, from literature):** Intentionally killing a living being
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-pc61
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
SuttaCentral identifies direct parallels to this rule across the extant Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṅghika traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, alongside the parallel nun's rule (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 142) [SuttaCentral]. In some non-Pali versions of the rule, the term *pāṇa* is explicitly glossed as animals (*tiryagyonigata*) [Schmithausen 1991b]. DharmaNexus detects 323 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 78 texts, sharing extensive formulaic legal phrases with rules such as Pācittiya 45, Pācittiya 30, Saṅghādisesa 5, and Pārājika 3, as well as automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) and *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
